name: TCH burnToken signature replay through v-byte malleability
summary: TCH.burnToken() burns a share of the TCH/USDT pair's TCH and syncs when given an authorizedSigner signature, and blocks replays by the keccak256 of the raw signature bytes, while splitSignature adds 27 to any v below 27. The attacker resubmitted the operator's already-used signatures with v rewritten from 27/28 to 0/1, so each passed as new; with flash-loaned USDT it bought TCH, burned the pair's TCH repeatedly, and sold back into the shrunken reserve.
notes: Reset is the owner's setUniswapV2Pair (slot 0xf), 212 blocks after deployment and after setAuthorizedSigner (slot 0x13): burnToken burns from and syncs that pair, so the exploit needed it (rule 8).

Campaign: every burnToken call by a party other than the operator 0x6117ef8c, whose 35 calls before the anchor all carry v 27 or 28. Copycat 0xb50d320f's seven replay burns moved no USDT themselves; the same-block buys and sells by other accounts around them are not counted. Loss is the pair's net USDT outflow per transaction (loss.mjs); its TCH is valued at nothing (rule 12).
